newsitem.title: CHILE: Ecuador crisis shows Latam democracy fragile - Chile.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador crisis shows Latam democracy fragile - Chile.

text.p: The political crisis in Ecuador following the ouster of president Abdala Bucaram highlights the delicacy of Latin American democracies, Chilean Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza said on Friday.
"I think what happened in Ecuador is not normal, is something that no one wants to happen, and shows we still have vacuums and fragility in our democratic systems," he said.
Last week's sudden sacking of Bucaram by lawmakers amid a 48-hour national strike set a bad precedent for the region, he told reporters.

The crisis sparked by Bucaram's dismissal was resolved on Tuesday when new President Fabian Alarcon was sworn in by Congress after days of confusion during which three candidates battled for the presidency.
The Group of Rio, which links 14 Latin American nations, will continue to analyse the events in Ecuador with a view to reaching a consensus "and issuing a collective opinion," Insulza said.
Insulza said group members had closed ranks over the Ecuador crisis even though some had shown support for Bucaram.
"All consider that was happened was negative, but at the same time, the majority recognise that there is a consolidated interim government in Ecuador," he said.
